chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali and Abu Qatadah al-Qummi, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about the funeral prayer when the sun turns red (at sunset), is it valid or not? He said, 'There is no prayer during the time of a prayer.' And he said, 'When the sun sets, pray Maghrib, then pray over the funeral bodies.'

key_terms.وَقْتِ صَلَاةٍ: Time of a prayer (specifically the time of no prayer)

ai.seo_question: When should funeral prayers be performed if they coincide with sunset?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for funeral prayers during the time of sunset (Ishraq), specifically when the sun is red, by prioritizing the obligatory Maghrib prayer to avoid the 'no prayer' period. It establishes a practical hierarchy where the wajib Maghrib takes precedence over the sunnah funeral prayer, ensuring the obligatory duty is fulfilled before attending to the deceased. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining the integrity of the five daily prayers even when concurrent with other acts of worship.
